clue.text: Use this to get into training for the doctors' dance?

definitions.text: Use this to get into training
definitions.note: a description of the equipment rather than a synonym
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a heavy ball thrown about in fitness work

definitions.note: cryptic: a ball held by the medical profession
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read literally: a formal party, a ball, thrown by the medical profession

explanation.surface: Someone hunting for the right kit to get fit, then asked if a doctors' party would do.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun: the same two words name heavy exercise equipment and, read literally, a dance held by physicians.
explanation.definitionFit: A weighted exercise ball is standard training equipment, while a ball is also a formal dance and medicine is the doctors' profession.

clue.text: Horse without carriage — how ghastly!

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one word wraps around the other

parts.note: a female horse
a cab was a horse-drawn carriage for hire

explanation.surface: A horse with no carriage to pull, and an onlooker exclaiming at how dreadful it is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but here it means outside: the carriage sits inside the horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Macabre describes something gruesome and death-haunted, a close synonym for grisly or horrible.

clue.text: Benefactor's name is in the entrance

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a door is the way in to a room or building
N is the standard abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A patron's name is carved over the doorway of the building they funded.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'is': N placed in DOOR gives DONOR. The OCR lost this clue, but the scan shows it.
explanation.definitionFit: A donor gives money or goods to a cause, which is exactly what a benefactor does: a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Terrier to advance over jolly mountainous area

parts.note: a cairn is a small Scottish terrier
to go forward
a jolly is slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM

explanation.surface: A dog being urged forward across some cheerful hill country.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'over' just places the first pieces above the last one. A jolly is old naval slang for a Royal Marine.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cairngorms are a range of high mountains in the Scottish Highlands, a mountainous region.

clue.text: Chap, age up to 50

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading the word from the bottom to the top

parts.note: an eon is an age, a vast span of time
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A man described as being aged up to fifty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up to 50' reads like an age range; split it, so 'up' turns the age round and 'to' adds the fifty.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel is a man's first name, and crosswords use chap to stand for any male forename.

clue.text: Dutch creature resembling a bird

parts.note: a bat is a flying creature
avian means of or like birds

explanation.surface: A Dutch animal described as looking like a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: Batavia was the Latin name for the Netherlands, so Batavian is an old word for Dutch.
explanation.definitionFit: Batavian is a historical adjective for the Netherlands and its people, from the Roman province there.

clue.text: Admirer gets nothing right

parts.note: love is a score of nothing in tennis
the usual abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A suitor who gets nothing right.
explanation.walkthrough: Nothing is the tennis zero here rather than the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: A lover is someone devoted to another, an admirer or sweetheart in the romantic sense.

clue.text: Learn to dance for market day

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
the Argentine dance

explanation.surface: An instruction to learn a dance in time for a day at the market.
explanation.walkthrough: On the old London Stock Exchange, contango day was the settlement day on which deferred payment was arranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Contango day was a fixed date in the Stock Exchange account when charges for postponing settlement were agreed.

clue.text: French author accepts parking in university grounds

indicators.note: to accept is to take something in, so the author's name holds the other piece

parts.note: Albert Camus, French novelist
P is the sign for a car park

explanation.surface: A French writer allowing cars to park on a college site.
explanation.definitionFit: A campus is the land and buildings belonging to a university or college.

clue.text: Temperate land mass

definitions.meaning: second meaning: one of the great divisions of dry land on Earth

explanation.surface: A large region of the globe with a mild climate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Temperate land mass' reads as one climate description, but temperate here means moderate in behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means restrained in appetite or passion; as a noun it names a large mass of land like Europe.

clue.text: Shakespearian heroine takes a bow

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the disguised heroine of Twelfth Night

definitions.note: a description of the instrument, which is played with a bow
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a stringed instrument played with a bow

explanation.surface: An actress playing a Shakespeare heroine taking her curtain call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes a bow' sounds like applause at the theatre, but the bow is the one drawn across strings.
explanation.definitionFit: Viola is the heroine of Twelfth Night, and the viola is the stringed instrument a little larger than a violin, bowed to play.

clue.text: Taking off Maurice the writer

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the surname of the English author Maurice, a novelist and poet

explanation.surface: A writer called Maurice heading off somewhere, or perhaps doing an impression.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking off suggests departing or mimicking; here it means stripping. Maurice Baring was an Edwardian English man of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Baring is the present participle of bare, to uncover, and also the family name of the writer Maurice Baring.

clue.text: Pass beyond the place for the bride's carriage?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: go past a limit

definitions.text: the place for the bride's carriage
definitions.note: cryptic: read as two words, over step
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read as two words: a bride is carried across the doorstep of her new home

explanation.surface: Going past the spot where a bride's coach should stand.
explanation.walkthrough: The carriage is not a vehicle but the act of carrying: tradition has the groom lift the bride across the threshold.
explanation.definitionFit: To overstep is to exceed a boundary; split, it describes the bride borne across the step at the door.

clue.text: Bond, held by the Third Man inside, saves Crown jewels

definitions.text: Bond, held by the Third Man

indicators.note: inside says the letters sit within the run of words that follows

parts.note: found spanning the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A spy thriller: a bond held by a mysterious figure who rescues the Crown jewels.
explanation.walkthrough: The Third Man suggests the film, but here it is simply a third party who holds a deed until conditions are met.
explanation.definitionFit: An escrow is a deed or bond kept by an independent third party until specified conditions are fulfilled.

clue.text: Brood in Colorado mountain pass, it appears

parts.note: the US state abbreviation

indicators.note: in tells us one piece is placed inside another here

parts.note: a gate is a narrow pass between hills
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sulking somewhere in the Rocky Mountains, so it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: To brood is to ponder at length, as is to cogitate, meaning to think deeply.

clue.text: Surgeon recognised skeleton

parts.note: saw in the sense of perceived or recognised
a skeleton is a set of bones

explanation.surface: A surgeon identifying a skeleton.
explanation.definitionFit: Sawbones is jocular slang for a doctor, especially a surgeon who amputates.

clue.text: Married poet in favour of a bit of brass

indicators.note: in tells us the first two pieces go inside the last

parts.note: a boon is a favour
M is the abbreviation for married
a bard is a poet

explanation.surface: A wedded poet who is keen on a little brass, whether money or metal.
explanation.walkthrough: A bit of brass sounds like money, but it is one instrument of the brass section.
explanation.definitionFit: A bombardon is a bass tuba used in military bands, one member of the brass instrument family.

clue.text: He dictates to a curate detailed letters

indicators.note: the letters are to be used as raw material and rearranged
de-tailed means having the tail cut off, so the final letter goes

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone dictating letters to a clergyman, in great detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed letters' reads as thorough correspondence; split it, 'detailed' docks the clergyman's last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An autocrat rules alone with absolute power, a dictator who lays down the law.

clue.text: Married once too often, so great love affairs right out

parts.note: big means great

indicators.note: out means removed, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: amours are love affairs
the usual abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A person wed too many times and having grand romances, with all propriety gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Bigamy is having two spouses at once, so a bigamous person has gone through a wedding one time more than allowed.

clue.text: Only an egghead would use such fuel

parts.note: but in the sense of merely or only
taken as written

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only the leading letter is kept

parts.note: read as egg plus head: the head, or opening letter, of egg

explanation.surface: A dig at intellectuals: only a brainbox would burn this kind of fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egghead' looks like one word for an intellectual; split it to take the head of egg.
explanation.definitionFit: This flammable hydrocarbon gas is sold in canisters for camping stoves, lighters and heaters.

clue.text: Lines perhaps capturing the royal bearing

indicators.note: to capture is to hold something within, so the second piece goes inside

parts.note: an impot, short for imposition, is a school punishment such as writing lines
R is the abbreviation for royal

explanation.surface: Lines of verse, perhaps, catching a regal manner.
explanation.walkthrough: An impot is British school slang for a punishment task; lines, copying a sentence over and over, are one example, hence 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: Import here means meaning or significance, as does bearing in the sense of relevance to a matter.

clue.text: Fix broadcast in support of roof

parts.note: to tie is to fasten or fix
to beam is to transmit a signal

explanation.surface: Mending a broadcast, perhaps a radio mast, to keep a roof up.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie-beam is the horizontal timber joining the feet of rafters, holding a roof structure together.

clue.text: Animal, four-footed and toed, stumbles round snare

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the jumbled letters wrap the next piece
something that stumbles loses its proper order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
a snare is a trap

explanation.surface: A four-legged creature tripping over a hunter's snare.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetrapod is any vertebrate with four limbs; the name is Greek for four feet.

clue.text: A rook, one up a tree

parts.note: taken as written
R is the chess notation for rook

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: an ace counts as one

explanation.surface: A rook bird perched in a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The rook is the chess piece, not the bird sitting up in the branches.
explanation.definitionFit: The areca is a tropical palm, the source of the betel nut, so it is a kind of tree.

clue.text: Scottish Cup _- that's on the news agency

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after, so the piece before this word goes second

parts.note: TASS was the Soviet news agency
i.e., Latin id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A news agency reporting on the Scottish Cup football competition.
explanation.walkthrough: The Scottish Cup sounds like the football trophy, but it is a Scots word for a small drinking cup.
explanation.definitionFit: Tassie is a Scots diminutive for a cup or goblet, as in Burns's 'fill it in a silver tassie'.

clue.text: Way above the atmosphere in part of the flight

indicators.note: in a down clue, above means written on top, so the first piece comes first

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
air is the atmosphere

explanation.surface: A route high above the atmosphere during a plane journey.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'above' puts the first piece on top of the second. The flight is a flight of steps, not an aeroplane trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A stair is a single step, and a flight is a run of steps between floors.

clue.text: Dentist's drill makes one speak indistinctly

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the small rotary cutting tool a dentist uses

definitions.note: a description of the accent, a noun, rather than a verb
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a rough, rolled pronunciation of r, as in some regional accents

explanation.surface: The dentist's drill leaves the patient mumbling.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the tiny dental cutting bit and a throaty regional accent that blurs speech.

clue.text: Chemical inter-reaction

indicators.note: a reaction rearranges elements into a new compound, so the letters are reassembled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A chemistry term for substances reacting with each other.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphenated word looks like one technical term; split it into the fodder and its signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitre is potassium nitrate, saltpetre, a chemical used in gunpowder and fertiliser.

clue.text: Golf, presumably — any number can play it

definitions.meaning: first meaning, playful: golf is played in rounds, so it is a game of rounds

definitions.note: a description of the game rather than a synonym
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a game with no fixed number of players, each playing for themselves

explanation.surface: Golf described as a game open to any number of players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Presumably' admits the joke: golf is not really what the term means, it just involves rounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A round game is a party game, often cards, in which players compete individually and the number taking part is open.

clue.text: A swinging gate-crasher

parts.note: surface reading: a fashionable, uninvited party guest from the swinging sixties
setter's reading: a heavy beam swung back and forth to smash in a castle gate

explanation.surface: A trendy, carefree type turning up uninvited at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: Swinging suggests hip and lively, but here it describes the beam's pendulum motion as it is driven at a gate.
explanation.definitionFit: A siege engine of a heavy log swung against doors literally crashes through gates.
